paper_metadata.title: Non-Differentiable Learning of Quantum Circuit Born Machine with Genetic Algorithm

summary: This paper studies a 12-qubit quantum circuit Born machine with 84 trainable rotation parameters, trained by a genetic algorithm on two financial datasets: 5,000 synthetic mixture samples and 4,382 USD/JPY log-return samples. On dataset 1, the QCBM achieved objective function 30.5 ± 23.6 over 100 runs versus 39.6 ± 30.8 for the RBM baseline, but the experiments were run on the Qiskit simulator and the authors explicitly do not claim demonstrated quantum advantage.

experiments.description: QCBM trained with a genetic algorithm to generate synthetic market data from two financial datasets, compared against an RBM baseline; experiments run in simulation with Qiskit.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) trained with a genetic algorithm
algorithm.ansatz: Hardware-efficient parameterized quantum circuit with alternating layers of adjustable 1-qubit rotations and fixed 2-qubit entangling gates; 12-qubit, 7 adjustable gates per qubit, two layers of fixed 2-qubit gates
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Randomly draw each rotation angle from the uniform distribution over the discrete angle set defined by m

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: rotation angles in [-pi, pi) discretized into 2^m values

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous samples are converted to 12-digit binary representation; each data sample is represented by M-digit binary numbers per variable, with M=12 in the experiments
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize squared distance between sorted training samples u and generated samples v(theta_hat): F(theta_hat)=sum_k (u_k - v_k(theta_hat))^2

problem_instance.description: Generative modeling of financial return distributions: a spiky light-tailed synthetic mixture distribution and a heavy-tailed USD/JPY spot FX log-return distribution
problem_instance.dataset_name: Mixture of four normal distributions, USD-JPY spot FX daily log-returns

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Convert continuous samples to 12-digit binary representation; generate 5000 samples for dataset 1 and 4382 samples for dataset 2

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: For each variable, compute min/max on training data, map real values to integers, then binarize into M-digit binary features; reverse mapping used for generated samples
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 runs for objective-function statistics; 20 GA runs for convergence plots; compare QCBM against RBM using PDF/QQ plots and objective-function mean/std

implementation_details.classical_solver: Scikit-learn BernoulliRBM for baseline; GA implemented classically
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Convert real-valued data to binary features; RBM trained with contrastive divergence
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert generated binary outputs back to real-valued samples

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: decreasing with diminishing returns as mutation rate decays

results.unit: mean ± std for QCBM(12,7) on dataset 1
mean ± std for RBM(12,7) on dataset 1

speedup_claims.factor: single circuit run vs 10^3-10^4 forward/backward passes
speedup_claims.conditions: for generating an independent sample from the learned distribution; ignoring readout and other overheads
speedup_claims.caveats: Presented as a qualitative argument for potential speed-up, not an empirical benchmark in this paper.

speedup_claims.conditions: if QCBM is trained effectively on NISQ hardware
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly states that the results do not constitute evidence of quantum advantage.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 12 qubits, 84 variational parameters, simulator-only execution, 100-run objective statistics, 20 GA convergence runs
limiting_factors: No demonstrated empirical quantum advantage over the classical RBM baseline
Classical RBM baseline is competitive and sometimes worse, but the paper does not establish a meaningful crossover size
Training relies on a classical genetic algorithm and simulator-based circuit evaluation

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states QCBM runs were performed on the Qiskit simulator and no real QPU is named.
